title: Tenali Raman and the Brinjals
summary: The king bans brinjals; Tenali feeds his horse brinjal curry and presents the dung as proof horses love them too.
moral: Wit can overturn even royal decrees

title: Tenali Raman and the Thieves
summary: Tenali tricks thieves into carrying his heavy trunk to the police station thinking it contains treasure.
moral: A clever mind turns enemies into servants

acts.name: trick
acts.summary: Tenali pretends trunk is full of gold

title: The Biggest Fool in the Kingdom
summary: King asks Tenali to find the biggest fool; Tenali brings a donkey and proves the king is the biggest fool for buying a bad horse.
moral: The wise can see folly even in royalty

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: King orders search for biggest fool

acts.name: reveal
acts.summary: Proves king was fooled by horse trader

title: Tenali Raman and the Cat
summary: Tenali drinks hot milk by pouring it from cup to cup; teaches patience in an indirect way.
moral: Patience finds a way through any problem

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Hot milk too hot to drink quickly

acts.name: solution
acts.summary: Tenali pours back and forth to cool

title: The Reward of a Million Gold Coins
summary: King promises a million gold coins; Tenali proves paying is harder than promising by asking for double each day starting from one grain of rice.
moral: Promises are easy; fulfillment is what matters

acts.name: request
acts.summary: Tenali asks for doubling grains on chessboard

title: Tenali and the Weight of the King's Problems
summary: King says his problems weigh a ton; Tenali brings actual weights and asks king to distribute problems among them.
moral: Sharing burdens makes them lighter

acts.name: wisdom
acts.summary: King learns to delegate and share burdens

title: The Rooster and the Precious Stones
summary: Tenali shows a rooster ignoring gems to eat grain, teaching the king that value depends on the beholder.
moral: True value is determined by need, not by rarity

acts.name: debate
acts.summary: King argues gems are most valuable

title: Tenali Raman and the Three Dolls
summary: Tenali solves the puzzle of three identical dolls — one is wise, one is foolish, one is evil — using a thread through the ears.
moral: The wise absorb knowledge; the foolish let it pass through; the evil spread it

acts.name: solution
acts.summary: Thread path reveals each doll's nature

title: The Horse Made of Butter
summary: Tenali is asked to bring a horse to life from a painting; he asks the king to first provide a real horse-shaped butter mold.
moral: An impossible demand deserves an equally impossible counter-demand

title: Tenali and the Mango Offering
summary: Tenali proves that the greedy priest only accepts the biggest mango, not the sweetest, exposing his materialism.
moral: Greed reveals itself through choices

acts.name: test
acts.summary: Tenali offers small sweet and large sour mangoes

title: The Invisible Cloth
summary: Weavers claim to make cloth visible only to intelligent people; Tenali exposes the fraud.
moral: Fear of appearing foolish makes people accept lies

acts.name: pretense
acts.summary: Everyone pretends to see the cloth

title: Tenali and the Wrestler
summary: A massive wrestler challenges anyone to fight him; Tenali brings his 'mother' (a huge woman) as his second.
moral: Brains defeat brawn when applied creatively

acts.name: retreat
acts.summary: Wrestler flees imagining the son's strength

title: The King's New Baby
summary: Courtiers flatter the ugly baby; Tenali honestly says the baby is healthy, which is what truly matters.
moral: Honest truth is more valuable than empty flattery

title: Tenali and the Wells
summary: Tenali proves a fraudulent astrologer wrong by asking him to predict which well has water.
moral: True knowledge can be tested; false claims crumble under scrutiny

acts.name: test
acts.summary: Tenali challenges with a practical test

title: The Greatest Pundit
summary: Tenali wins a debate against a visiting scholar by asking unanswerable questions about common things.
moral: Everyday wisdom is as important as scholarly knowledge

title: Tenali Saves the Gardener
summary: A gardener accidentally breaks a rare plant; Tenali breaks all the others so no one plant stands out.
moral: Sometimes the best solution is the most unexpected one

acts.name: solution
acts.summary: Tenali makes all plants look equal

title: The Bone in the Haystack
summary: Tenali finds a needle in a haystack by burning it and using a magnet on the ashes.
moral: Creative thinking solves what brute effort cannot

acts.name: solution
acts.summary: Tenali burns hay and uses magnet

title: Tenali and the Tax Collector
summary: Tenali disguises himself as a poor man and demonstrates to the king how corrupt tax collectors exploit the poor.
moral: True justice requires seeing problems firsthand

title: The Red Horse
summary: King wants a red horse; Tenali agrees but asks for a non-blue, non-white, non-black stable — proving the demand is impossible.
moral: The best way to refuse is to show why the request is impossible

title: Tenali Raman's Last Wish
summary: Before his death, Tenali plants a jasmine bush over a treasure to ensure his family discovers it while tending the plant.
moral: Wisdom endures beyond a lifetime

acts.name: instructions
acts.summary: Asks family to water the jasmine daily

acts.name: discovery
acts.summary: Family finds treasure under the plant
